question.problem:
The parabola $y={x}^{2}+5x+1$ and the line $y=3x$ intersect at the point $P.$ Find the coordinates of $P.$

The coordinates of $P$ are
$(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system consisting of the equations of the curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y={x}^{2}+5x+1 \\ y=3x\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5x+1 & =3x \\ {x}^{2}+5x+1-3x & =0 \\ {x}^{2}+2x+1 & =0 \\ (x+1)(x+1) & =0 \\ x & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of the intersection point is $x=-1.$

To find the $y$-coordinate of the intersection point, we plug this value into either curve. Let's choose the equation of the line. Substituting $x=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =3x \\  & =3(-1) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only point of intersection is $(-1,-3).$
